findings.claim: The patch removes the .lower() call that was part of normalize's existing contract, so inputs with uppercase characters are returned with original case instead of lowercased.
findings.evidence: service.py line 4 now returns value.strip() instead of value.strip().lower(). Verification run of tests/test_regression.py fails: assert normalize(" HELLO ") == "hello" produces AssertionError: assert 'HELLO' == 'hello'.
findings.verification: Run `pytest -q tests/test_regression.py`; test_normalize_preserves_lowercase_contract fails because normalize(" HELLO ") returns "HELLO" rather than "hello".

submission.summary: The patch adds None handling but drops the pre-existing lowercase normalization, breaking the established normalize contract. The new None behavior passes, but the existing regression test fails because uppercase input is no longer lowercased.
